summary: The petition challenged the validity of certain provisions of Madhya Pradesh local body laws permitting the State Government to determine ward boundaries, arguing that this undermined the independence of the State Election Commission. The Court found that despite ongoing delimitation or non-completion of the 'triple test' for OBC reservations, elections cannot be delayed beyond the constitutional five-year term mandate under Articles 243-E and 243-U. Over 23,000 local bodies in Madhya Pradesh were functioning without elected representatives, violating constitutional norms. The Court directed the State Election Commission to issue an election programme within two weeks based on the latest delimitation before the amendments or when elections became due, whichever was later, and to conduct elections without waiting for OBC reservation formalities. General category elections were to proceed if OBC reservations were not yet finalized.
legal_provisions_cited: Vikas Kishanrao Gawali Vs. State of Maharashtra
Kishansing Tomar Vs. Municipal Corporation of the City of Ahmedabad & Ors.
final_judgment: The Supreme Court directed the Madhya Pradesh State Election Commission to issue an election programme within two weeks based on the existing ward delimitation and to conduct elections without delay, ensuring elected bodies are installed before or immediately after the expiry of the five-year term, without waiting for completion of delimitation or OBC reservation formalities.
